subject: ent
title: Diseases of the external ear

steps.tx: The external ear collects sound through the pinna and external canal to the drum, with an outer cartilaginous part carrying glands with hair and an inner bony part that hurts easily. Congenital **atresia**, prominent ears and microtia affect appearance and **hearing development** in children. The bony inner canal explains severe pain patterns, while birth canal defects need early audiology with **appearance** counselling.
steps.say: The pinna and canal funnel sound toward the drum, which is their role in hearing. The outer canal carries glands and hair while the inner bony part feels pain sharply. Birth defects of the canal affect appearance and hearing growth. Early audiology with family counselling is the guide for these children. Pain patterns follow the bony tenderness closely.

steps.tx: Otitis externa inflames canal skin, often after water exposure or cotton bud trauma, causing itch then severe pain worsened by tragus pressure or jaw movement. Discharge with canal swelling and debris blocks hearing temporarily. **Pseudomonas** dominates swimmers and diabetics, while Aspergillus with Candida causes itchy fungal disease with visible spores after prolonged topical **antibiotics**. Treat with aural toilet, topical therapy and **tragus tenderness** mapping.
steps.say: Swimmer ear starts with itch and moves to severe pain on pressure. Water exposure and cotton buds injure canal skin before infection sets in, which is typical. Pseudomonas follows water while fungi follow prolonged topical antibiotics. Tragus pressure reproduces the pain sharply, which is diagnostic. Treatment is centred on cleaning with topical therapy and dry ear care.

steps.tx: This otoscopic view shows swollen erythematous canal walls with purulent **discharge**, arrows marking oedema, discharge and outer canal zones plus an external inset. The narrowed swollen canal with infected debris explains conductive **hearing loss** with severe **tragus tenderness**. Treat with aural toilet plus topical therapy, keep the ear dry, and reserve systemic cover for diabetics or spreading disease.
steps.say: This otoscopic view is a display of classic swimmer ear that is ready for the exam. Red swollen walls narrow the canal with yellow discharge pooled inside, which is typical. Arrows are markers of oedema, discharge and canal zones for orientation. Pain on tragus pressure with temporary deafness completes the picture, which is classic. Cleaning with topical therapy and dry ear care is the treatment.

vis.caption: Otoscopy showing swollen erythematous canal with purulent discharge. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Impacted wax needs treatment only when symptomatic with blockage, deafness or masked drum views, removed by syringing only with an intact drum and no infection history, or by microsuction with instruments under vision. **Auricular haematoma** from trauma needs drainage with compression, otherwise repeated bleeding destroys cartilage into **cauliflower ear**. Never syringe a perforated drum blindly, and confirm **intact drum** before irrigation.
steps.say: Wax is removed only when it blocks hearing or hides the drum. Syringing is suited to intact drums without infection while microsuction is suited to viewed clearance. A perforated drum is never irrigated blindly. Trauma haematomas need drainage with compression to save shape. Repeated bleeding without drainage destroys cartilage into cauliflower ear, which is permanent.

steps.tx: Malignant necrotising otitis externa means skull base **osteomyelitis** of the canal in elderly diabetics or immunosuppressed patients, almost always pseudomonal. Nocturnal deep pain, granulations at the bone cartilage junction and cranial nerve **palsies** signal spread beyond skin. It demands prolonged antipseudomonal **therapy** with imaging, never simple ear drops alone, and urgent referral when night pain meets granulations.
steps.say: Deep night pain in an elderly diabetic with canal granulations is typical of skull base infection. This disease spreads beyond skin into bone and nerves. Facial weakness follows as the infection advances. Simple ear drops never control this stage. Systemic antipseudomonal therapy with imaging and referral is the decider of the outcome.

vis.alt: Illustration of malignant otitis externa showing granulations in the ear canal at the bone-cartilage junction and facial asymmetry due to cranial nerve palsy.
vis.caption: Malignant otitis externa: granulations at bone-cartilage junction, facial palsy

steps.tx: Perichondritis infects pinna cartilage after trauma, piercing or burns, sparing the **lobule** which has no cartilage, while relapsing polychondritis stays autoimmune and recurrent. Canal **furuncle** means staphylococcal abscess of the outer canal hair follicle with focal tenderness. Herpes zoster oticus or Ramsay Hunt blisters the concha with facial palsy when varicella zoster reactivates in the **geniculate ganglion**.
steps.say: Lobule sparing points to cartilage disease of the pinna. Trauma, piercing or burns infect cartilage while the lobule is spared. Furuncles mark infected hair follicles of the outer canal, which is typical. Ramsay Hunt blisters the ear with facial palsy when shingles is reactivated. Relapsing polychondritis is autoimmune rather than infective and is recurrent.
